Fixes #609

## Problem

`src/clients/doctor.rs` capped Claude Code at 2.1.265, the version pinned in the real-client fixture. So `router with claude --resume <session>` (and `clients doctor claude`) exited before launch on Claude Code 2.1.283 with:

```
Claude Code 2.1.255 through 2.1.265 is required for the reviewed Router gateway model-discovery and authentication contract; installed version reports '2.1.283 (Claude Code)'
```

The fixture is a tested baseline, not a maximum. The credential boundary never depended on the version ceiling. Router only gives the child its own token and base URL, and Claude.ai-only operations are refused per operation by `unsupported_native_command`.

## Changes

- **Version gate** (`src/clients/doctor.rs`): removes the upper bound and keeps the 2.1.255 minimum needed for gateway alias resolution. The error for older clients now says "2.1.255 or newer is required …".
- **Fail-closed boundary kept** (`src/client_launch.rs`): `--cloud`, `--environment`, `--remote-control`/`--rc`, `--teleport`, `remote-control` and `ultrareview` are still refused for every release, before any server lookup, token mint or launch. The limitation text no longer ties itself to 2.1.265. It says "checked through 2.1.283". The installed 2.1.283 binary still contains the `API-key auth precedence active` / `takes precedence over your claude.ai login` logic from #520, so there is still no split-auth mechanism.
- **Real-client coverage** (`tests/real_clients_test.rs`, `.github/workflows/real-clients.yml`):
  - The Claude version under test can be overridden with `ROUTER_REAL_CLIENT_CLAUDE_VERSION` (default: the 2.1.265 baseline). The user-agent assertion is now version-generic.
  - A new `claude-newer-release` job runs the Claude capture against 2.1.283. It covers split auth (Router-only sampling and `/v1/models` credentials, stored Claude.ai login byte-identical, no OAuth token reaching Router, only a blocked pre-TLS CONNECT externally), native model discovery, the `/model` selector, and the privacy matrix.
  - On push, nightly and manual runs the job also runs against the moving `latest` tag. Pull requests stay pinned so upstream releases can't break unrelated PRs.
- **Docs and changelog**: README, `docs/use-cases/cli-claude-code.md`, `docs/use-cases/with-router.md`, plus a patch changelog fragment.

## Reproduction and tests

- New hermetic test `newer_claude_release_is_not_rejected_by_version_alone` (`tests/with_router/claude_profile_test.rs`). A fake Claude reporting `2.1.283` is launched with `claude --resume <id>`. **It fails on `main`** with the error above and passes with this change.
- New test `claude_below_the_gateway_alias_minimum_is_refused_before_router_access`: 2.1.252 is still refused, before any Router access.
- `explicit_claude_ai_operation_fails_before_router_access_or_client_launch` now runs for both 2.1.265 and 2.1.283.
- Unit test `newer_claude_releases_are_not_rejected_by_version_alone` covers 2.1.266, 2.1.283, 2.2.0 and 3.0.0.

Local runs:

```
# real Claude Code 2.1.283, before this change
ROUTER_REAL_CLIENT_TESTS=1 ROUTER_REAL_CLIENT_CLAUDE_VERSION=2.1.283 cargo test --test real_clients_test claude
  -> FAILED (Claude Code 2.1.255 through 2.1.265 is required …)
# after this change
  -> ok. 3 passed (native surface + split auth, model selector, privacy matrix)
# real Claude Code 2.1.265 baseline
ROUTER_REAL_CLIENT_TESTS=1 cargo test --test real_clients_test claude  -> ok. 3 passed
cargo test --locked      -> all passed
cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -> clean
```

body:
## Summary

Add one local client lifecycle interface for the eight supported clients: verified backup and merge-first restore, settings/full reset, and vendor-aware binary maintenance. The same profile inventory drives all three operations. Preserve the existing `router with --reset-to-default-configuration claude` spelling while changing it to a settings-only reset backed by a verified archive. Retire the internal whole-home replacement entry point so it cannot bypass verification.

## Requirements and implementation

| Issue | Requirement | Implementation and decision |
| --- | --- | --- |
| #604 | Independent backup, user-selected private destination, capacity check, clone/copy fallback | `clients backup create` accepts the default per-user directory or an absolute / `~/` destination, rejects destinations inside selected profiles, checks free bytes, uses `reflink-copy` with ordinary-copy fallback, and atomically publishes a verified manifest. Incomplete copies cannot be restored. |
| #604 | All client homes, overrides, session/project data and unavailable stores | Inventory covers all eight normal homes, Claude/Gemini Router-owned homes, separate OpenCode config/data and Qwen runtime stores, and documented root overrides. Missing stores are reported explicitly. Project-local files outside those roots remain outside the selected profile. |
| #604 | Consistent snapshot, links, metadata, credentials | Active client writers, Router-owned Claude session markers and concurrent Router operations are refused; copied files are checked against their sources, open SQLite sidecars and escaping links are refused, and modes and links are preserved. Known credential files are omitted by default; `--include-credentials` creates a private, unencrypted local backup. |
| #604 | Verify and safe restore | `verify` checks the manifest checksum, complete inventory, file size/hash/type/mode, symlinks, and an isolated sample restore. Restore defaults to an idempotent merge with deterministic conflict names. Overwrite requires `--yes` and creates a verified recovery backup before staged replacement. |
| #605 | Settings reset without losing sessions/auth; explicit full reset | `clients reset` removes only known settings files after a verified backup. `--full --yes` resets selected local stores, including sessions and local credentials, after a complete verified backup. Normal and Router-owned scopes stay separate. |
| #605 | Safe planning and diagnostics | Dry run/JSON report targets and categories. Malformed settings, active clients, symlink escapes and changed files block mutation. Ambient override names are reported without values; remote token revocation is never implied. |
| #606 | Install/update/reinstall across all eight | Dry run/JSON produces a per-client action or explicit unsupported reason. Existing install method is detected; supported npm, Homebrew and documented native vendor actions are used without implicit method/channel changes. Reinstall requires confirmation and a verified profile backup. Binary path/version are checked afterward, and changed binaries after failed vendor commands are reported as partial. |
| #607 | One PR closes all three child issues | This PR contains implementation, tests and documentation together. |

## Reproduction and verification

Before this change, `router clients backup`, `router clients reset`, and `router clients update` were absent. The old `router with --reset-to-default-configuration claude` moved the entire Router-owned Claude home away from the active profile, leaving prior sessions inaccessible there.

The new integration fixtures exercise every client with sessions, settings and auth; separate normal/Router-owned Claude profiles; merge idempotence and symlink conflicts; overwrite recovery; full reset; malformed settings; profile-root overrides; archive tampering; private archive permissions; successful and failed npm maintenance; native Claude update/reinstall; and path aliases during symlink restore. See `tests/clients_lifecycle_test.rs`, `tests/clients_maintenance_test.rs`, the Windows SID unit test, and the updated Claude wrapper regression. Run:

```sh
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo clippy --locked --all-targets --all-features
env -u CODEX_HOME cargo test --locked --all-features
rust-script scripts/check-file-size.rs
rust-script scripts/check-terminology.rs
rust-script scripts/check-changelog-fragment.rs
```

The runner for this PR sets `CODEX_HOME` to its own repository path; the pre-existing `subscription::tests::resolve_home_uses_subdir` assumes it is unset. Local full-suite verification therefore uses `env -u CODEX_HOME cargo test --locked --all-features`.

## Coverage review

This feature adds approximately 3,800 lines across new lifecycle paths. The repository line-coverage ratchet measured 85.21% on the first fully compiled CI run, versus the default-branch baseline of 85.51%. Additional integration tests for npm and native Claude maintenance and path-alias restore exercise critical positive and failure paths; the final local measurement is 85.251719% (61,741 / 72,422 lines), committed in `coverage-baseline.txt`. The existing `coverage-exception` label is applied so that this intentional, reviewable decrease follows `docs/test-coverage.md` and the 80% absolute floor remains enforced.

## Research and boundaries

The implementation follows the [Codex configuration reference](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/config-file/config-reference), [Claude setup guide](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/setup), [Gemini installation and configuration](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/main/docs/get-started/installation.mdx), [Qwen configuration](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/main/docs/users/configuration/settings.md), [Cursor CLI installation](https://docs.cursor.com/en/cli/installation), [OpenCode CLI](https://dev.opencode.ai/docs/cli/), and Microsoft's [Windows ACL commands](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/administration/windows-commands/icacls). Existing [reflink-copy](https://docs.rs/reflink-copy/latest/reflink_copy/) and [fs2](https://docs.rs/fs2/latest/fs2/) components supply clone/copy and space/locking primitives. [SQLite's online backup API](https://www.sqlite.org/backup.html) was considered for live databases; the local lifecycle instead refuses open write-ahead state and asks the user to close the client.

Archive transport remains the user's responsibility: backups are private but unencrypted, and a same-volume clone does not protect against disk loss. OS keychain entries and project-local files outside the documented profile roots are not claimed as backed up. Persistent Router-owned Windows profiles retain their existing `%USERPROFILE%/.config` path while normal client config/data use native application directories. An unknown install method/channel returns unsupported rather than guessing. Human-facing lifecycle text uses the repository's English CLI fallback; JSON safety states are stable across locales. More operational details and per-client paths are in `docs/client-lifecycle.md`.

Fixes #604
Fixes #605
Fixes #606
Fixes #607

body:
Closes #220.

`--help`, the `invalid value` error, `clients list` and the docs all advertised `claude-code`, `gemini-cli`, `grok-cli`, `qwen-code` and `cursor` — none of which is what the user's shell has. Someone who had just installed `claude` had no reason to guess the router called it `claude-code`, and the error message actively taught the wrong name. The short forms already worked as aliases; nothing announced them, because clap does not list aliases.

Canonical names are now the real commands. The descriptive forms are kept as aliases, so existing scripts and previously documented commands keep working.

```
before: [possible values: codex, claude-code, cursor, gemini-cli, grok-cli, opencode, qwen-code, agent]
after:  [possible values: codex, claude, cursor-agent, gemini, grok, opencode, qwen, agent]
```

## Two consequences the issue doesn't raise — the important part of this PR

**1. `Display` had to change too, and it names files on disk.**

`clients list` prints via `Display`, not the ValueEnum, so changing only the enum attributes would have left the list showing names the CLI no longer accepts — and the existing test would not have caught it, because `assert!(output.contains("cursor"))` still passes against `cursor-agent`.

But `Display` *also* derives the managed file paths — `<client>.env` and `<client>.credential.json`. Renaming it alone would have silently orphaned every existing installation's `claude-code.env`, and told the user to run a setup they had already run.

So an existing file under the previous name is still found, and only new installations use the canonical name. Both directions are tested, and I verified the fallback is load-bearing by removing it and watching the test fail.

**2. The `with` wrapper's argument-boundary list had already drifted.**

`src/cli/with.rs` carried a hand-written copy of the client names used to find where router flags end and client arguments begin. It had no entry for `cursor-agent` — so that client's arguments would not have been protected. It now derives the list from the client table, so it cannot fall out of step again.

Also: `Display` uses `f.pad`, so the fixed-width column in `clients list` still aligns. That is the same trap as #212, where `write_str` silently discarded the caller's requested width — `cursor-agent` is exactly 12 characters and would have collided with the next column.

## Tests

The invariant the issue asks for, as one assertion over the existing table:

- every variant's advertised name equals its `ClientIntegration::command`, checked through the ValueEnum, `Display` *and* `canonical_name()`, so no surface can drift from another. **Verified to fail on drift** — reverting one attribute produces `qwen-code is advertised but the command is qwen`;
- every legacy name (`claude-code`, `cursor`, `gemini-cli`, `grok-cli`, `qwen-code`) still parses, so this is not a breaking change;
- `clients list` shows the canonical names **and no longer shows the legacy ones** — the negative half matters, since substring matching hid the old behaviour;
- a managed file written under the legacy name is still found; a fresh installation uses the canonical name.

I also updated three existing tests that asserted the old filenames and list output. Those were correct failures, not incidental ones.

## Scope

I did **not** rename the `docs/use-cases/cli-*.md` files themselves. They are referenced from `README.md`, `docs/use-cases/README.md`, a `setup_limitation` string in `src/clients.rs`, and two changelog entries; renaming them is churn beyond what the issue asks, and the issue's item 3 is about names the CLI *shows*. The commands inside those docs are updated.

`SubscriptionProvider` (`claude-code`/`qwen-code` as vendor aliases in `src/subscription.rs`, `src/config.rs`) is a different enum and is untouched.

## Verification
885 tests pass, exit code 0. `cargo fmt`, `clippy --all-targets --all-features -D warnings`, CI's exact rustdoc command, and the file-size check are clean. `clients.rs` crossed the 1000-line limit, so its test module moved to `clients_tests.rs` using the `#[path]` pattern already used in this repo; no test content changed in the move.

Closes #548

## Summary
- preserve the exact requested Codex catalogue model ID in buffered native Responses payloads
- preserve that ID in every streamed Responses lifecycle object that already carries a model field
- retain byte-for-byte native transparency when no model rewrite or output limiting is needed
- cover every client-scoped advertised Codex model in local and protected live regression tests
- keep Router-specific headers and private fields off the public protocol

## Root cause
The native Codex path bypassed the existing Responses identity rewriter, so the provider-resolved model replaced an advertised alias in response.created and response.completed events.

## Verification
- cargo fmt --all -- --check

- existing native Codex transparency regression
- output-limit rewriter unit suite

- protected real-client workflow for Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Qwen, and OpenCode

## Dependency audit
All compatible repository dependencies were audited before merge. Cargo has no Rust 1.89-compatible lockfile updates; npm reports no outdated direct dependencies and zero vulnerabilities; pinned real clients, GitHub Actions, toolchain action, and Docker base digests are current.

body:
Completes all four child issues of #703 in this PR. Report operations now expose domain facts to Rust, JavaScript/TypeScript and Python; Claude's offline selector harness reconstructs terminal repaints; deployment inventories accept validated token-list envelopes; importing Rust applications select and validate the actual Router daemon.

### Changes and reproduction

- **#699:** Before, `doctor.data.status` was absent and report schemas exposed only output lines. Add eight public domain reports and typed Rust facades, regenerate all contracts and binding declarations, preserve human rendering separately, and correct the backup ID listing schema found during the 61-operation audit. Tests inspect provider acceptance/rejection, recommendations, deployments, client HTTP results, server selection, model identities and decoded log records without parsing `data.output`.
- **#700:** Reproduced the Claude Code 2.1.291 selector timeout with isolated synthetic credentials. ANSI stripping discarded cursor redraw semantics and mangled exact model IDs. Use `vt100` screen reconstruction and observed input readiness within existing finite deadlines. Preserve authorization withdrawal and exact outbound identity checks, strengthen Default display identity matching, and run two pinned 2.1.291 captures in CI alongside the existing baseline and 2.1.284 coverage.
- **#701:** A real Router 1.16.1 container → host → container round trip failed with `host token inventory is invalid`. All six deployment consumers now share typed decoding that validates operation/schema/success/exit status before reading envelope data, while retaining legacy arrays. Always-enabled regressions cover malformed/failed/mismatched envelopes and refusal before stopping the host; the real previous-image round trip passes.
- **#702:** The old host runtime selected an importing application's executable and reported the linked library version. Add `OperationContext.daemon_executable`, honor scoped `ROUTER_BIN`, validate the selected daemon's version contract, and use its actual version in plans, persisted state and convergence. A separate consumer rejecting Router CLI arguments exercises real plan/apply/status/stop with disposable state and a random loopback port, including explicit-path precedence. Preserve renamed Router CLI installations through version validation.
- Direct Rust facade regressions additionally check typed/untyped report parity and preserve domain facts on unsuccessful model/client/tunnel operations. The renamed-executable regression uses a directory symlink and checks the canonical path, including macOS temporary-directory aliases.
- Fix the existing contract compatibility CI crash when OpenAPI's boolean `required` was treated as a JSON Schema list; add its reproducing test. Add the minor changelog fragment required by the automatic release workflow.

The [complete requirements, research, alternatives and codebase audit](https://github.com/link-assistant/router/blob/issue-703-a399e1e39a55/docs/case-studies/issue-703/README.md) records every requirement and the corresponding implementation and verification. No child issue is deferred, already resolved or irreproducible.

### Validation

- Rust: 789 ordinary integration, binary and example tests passed; the separate Rust consumer completed real plan/apply/status/stop; 15 documentation tests passed; documentation builds with warnings denied. All 2,142 distinct unit tests passed in eight bounded local compiler shards, and their names exactly match the ordinary Linux CI suite. The combined unit-test compiler exceeds this workspace’s 3 GiB memory limit; CI runs the unchanged suite.
- The normally ignored 60-second soak also passed under a 2 GiB process memory cap: 770 requests, zero failures, bounded memory/tasks/file descriptors.
- Real container → host → container round trip against unchanged `ghcr.io/link-assistant/router:1.16.1` passed twice, including final product source.
- Two complete offline Claude Code 2.1.291 captures passed all five scenarios each, retaining exact identity and authorization withdrawal assertions.
- All nine Node, nine Bun and nine Python tests passed, along with strict TypeScript checking and JavaScript/Python distribution builds.
- Generated Java, Go and PHP clients compile and pass real Router runtime probes; all 349 documented HTTP operations are present.
- Formatting, Clippy across all targets/features, file-size/terminology checks, generated-contract/binding checks, published-contract compatibility against main and the six-consumer inventory audit passed.
- Final-head line coverage is 86.22%; the public Rust report facade helpers have 100% line coverage. The committed measured baseline is 86.221863%.
- The [first Windows attempt](https://github.com/link-assistant/router/actions/runs/37453288412/job/112236353964) exceeded the existing five-second PowerShell disk-capacity probe deadline (preserved first-attempt log lines 3598–3614). The [unchanged rerun](https://github.com/link-assistant/router/actions/runs/37453288412/job/112242355788) passed the complete Windows library, binary, integration and documentation suites; no deadline was increased.
- All seven current-head workflows passed on [`f473801`](https://github.com/link-assistant/router/commit/f47380144241791000657a494d19fba47416ca8b): [CI/CD Pipeline](https://github.com/link-assistant/router/actions/runs/37453288412), [Real Client Capture](https://github.com/link-assistant/router/actions/runs/37453288396), downstream bindings/contracts, Docker Runtime Build, upgrade matrix, benchmarks and fuzzing. The pipeline passed Linux/macOS/Windows tests, lint, coverage, optimized release compilation and Cargo package checks. All 31 applicable PR checks passed; 13 release-only or inapplicable checks were skipped.

Native client tests use synthetic tokens and loopback fixtures; this evidence covers native protocol, model identity and authorization behavior, without claiming live paid-provider acceptance. Full reproduction and verification logs are preserved locally, with CI diagnostics attached by the existing workflows.
